d: On June 10, 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi became the longest continuously serving democratically elected Prime Minister in India's history, surpassing Jawaharlal Nehru's record of 4,398 days. The milestone marks a significant moment in India's political journey, linking two leaders who governed vastly different versions of the country. From taking office in May 2014 to leading India through three consecutive election victories, the COVID-19 pandemic, global economic shocks, and a rapidly changing world order, Modi's tenure has coincided with a period of major transformation.
